ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of the hypotenuse $AB$, and $DE \perp AB$ intersects $AC$ at point $E$. If $AC=8$ and $BC=6$, then what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In right triangle $\triangle ABC$, we have
\[AB=\sqrt{AC^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}=10,\]
since point D is the midpoint of AB,
\[AD=\frac{1}{2}AB=5;\]
since DE$\perp$AB,
\[\angle ADE=\angle C=90^\circ,\]
and since $\angle A=\angle A$,
\[\triangle ADE\sim \triangle ACB,\]
hence
\[\frac{DE}{BC}=\frac{AD}{AC},\]
which gives
\[\frac{DE}{6}=\frac{5}{8}.\]
Solving this, we find $DE=\boxed{\frac{15}{4}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point A of triangle ABC is at the lower left, point C is at the lower right, and point B is at the upper right; AC is drawn as a horizontal line segment, and BC is drawn as a vertical line segment, so angle C is a right angle, and AB is the hypotenuse. Point D is located on the hypotenuse AB, point E is located on the base AC, and line segment DE connects from D to E, and there is a right-angle mark at D, indicating that DE is perpendicular to AB. Reasoning: From the problem, AC=8, BC=6, and triangle ABC is right-angled at C, so AB=sqrt(8^2+6^2)=sqrt(64+36)=10. D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB, therefore AD=AB/2=5. Because DE is perpendicular to AB, angle ADE=90 degrees; and because angle C=90 degrees, angle ADE=angle C. Also, AD is on AB and AE is on AC, therefore angle DAE is exactly angle A of triangle ABC, and the two triangles ADE and ACB have a common angle A. Therefore triangle ADE is similar to triangle ACB. The correspondence is AD corresponds to AC, DE corresponds to BC, so DE/BC=AD/AC. Substituting BC=6, AD=5, AC=8, we get DE/6=5/8, therefore DE=6*5/8=30/8=15/4.
